sentences.text: 1 1. The Court proceedings have been conducted through Video-Conferencing in view of the present scenario so as to maintain social distancing.
Page No.# 2/5 2.
I have heard Mr. P. Mahanta, learned counsel for the petitioners, and Mr. N. J. Dutta, learned Additional Public Prosecutor, Assam, appearing for the respondent.

3. Sri Arvind Goel, Smti. Kirti Goel, Sri Abhishek Goel and Sri Deepak Poddar have filed this petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, challenging the proceedings initiated vide C.R. Case No. 2183c/2001, pending in the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kamrup,
Guwahati (transferred to the Court of Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate (II), Sadar, Guwahati).

sentences.text: The petitioners have also challenged orders dated 20.02.2002 and 31.10.2011, passed by the Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate (II), Sadar, Guwahati.
4. It appears that a complaint under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short, "Act of 1954") was filed.
In course of the proceedings, on 20.02.2002, Summons were issued to summon the accused and the case was fixed for 08.04.2002.
On perusal of the order-sheet, it appears that on 08.04.2002 again Summons were ordered to be issued.

5. It appears that two petitions, bearing No. 5781 and 5780 were filed in view of Section 17(4) of the Act of 1954, while taking the plea that the proceedings cannot be initiated against the accused and the prosecution has failed to establish that the offending acts were committed with the consent and connivance of the accused, who happen to be the Directors of M/s Itrik Industries Pvt. Ltd. involved in manufacturing of Bisleri Mineral Water.

6. Order dated 31.10.2011, which is also under challenge, reads as under:
"Accuseds are absent with steps.
Petitions 5781 & 5780 are allowed.
The ld.

Counsel for the accused submitted that in view of Section 17(4), the case cannot proceed against the accuseds as the prosecution has failed to established that the act was committed with the consent or connivance of the accuseds.
Perused the materials and record.

It appears that the complaint has been filed against all the Directors, the company and its production managers alleging that they were responsible for the conducts of the business on the date of occurrence and after obtaining consent from the Joint Directors of the Health Services, Kamrup Guwahati.

Section 17(2) of the P.F.A. Act 1954 says that any company may, by order in Page No.# 3/5 writing, authorize any of its directors or managers to exercise all such powers and take all such steps as may be necessary or expedient to prevent the Arvind Goel And 3 Ors vs State Of Assam on 28 May, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34670044/
2 commission by the Company of any offence under this act and may give notice to the Local (Health) Authority.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But where no person has been so nominated, every person who at time the offence was committed was in charge of, and was responsible to, the company for the conduct of the business of the company and the company shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly (Section 17).

This has also been held in the reported case of R. Banerjee and Others- Vs- H.D.
Dubey and others- (1992) 2 SCC 552.

Dubey and others- (1992) 2 SCC 552
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case as there was no such nomination all the persons responsible for the conduct of the business has been named as accused and the case will proceed against all of them.
Hence the submission made by the Ld. Counsel cannot be accepted.
Fixing 4-1-12 for C.C."

6. Sub-Section (2) of Section 17 of the Act of 1954 reads as under:
"(2) Any company may, by order in writing, authorise any of its directors or managers (such manager being employed mainly in a managerial or supervisory capacity) to exercise all such powers and take all such steps as may be necessary or expedient to prevent the commission by the company of any offence under this Act and may give notice to the Local (Health) Authority, in such form and in such manner as may be prescribed, that it has nominated such director or manager as the person responsible,
along with the written consent of such director or manager for being so nominated.
Explanation.--Where a company has different establishments or branches or different units in any establishment or branch, different persons may be nominated under this sub-section in relation to different establishments or branches or units and the person nominated in relation to any establishment, branch or unit shall be deemed to be the person responsible in respect of such establishment, branch or unit."
7.

It appears that the Magistrate took cognizance of the statutory provisions to record that the company had not nominated any person under Section 17(2) of the Act of 1954 and, Page No.# 4/5 therefore, the offence would be deemed to have been committed by the persons who were in charge of the affairs of the company.
8.
I find that the affidavit in support of the petition was sworn on 20.03.2012 by Sri Arvind Goel.

Additional affidavit was filed by Sri Arvind Goel, which was sworn on 24.04.2012, i.e.,
approximately after one month, to bring on record a report dated 07.07.2001, furnished by Public Analyst, and another report dated 13.02.2002, furnished by Central Food Laboratory.

sentences.text:
An attempt has been made to convince the Court that in view of the different conclusions drawn vide the two reports, one dated 07.07.2001 (supra) and the other dated 13.02.2002 (supra), the complaint cannot be proceeded with.
9.
I find that the two reports are contradictory.
However, the grounds of challenge do not include the ground of contradictory reports.
I am constrained on observing that although the petition was filed in the year 2012, however, the reports relating to the years 2001 and 2002 were not brought to the notice of the Court.

Evidently, the reports came in light a decade before filing of the petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
10.
Be that as it may, learned counsel for the petitioners contends that let the presence of the accused persons be exempted.

The accused would take all the pleas available to them in law and in facts before the learned trial Court, including on the basis of the two reports dated 07.07.2001 (supra) and 13.02.2002 (supra).
11.
The Court has been informed that the petitioners are already on bail.

12. Considering the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case, personal appearance of the petitioners during the course of the proceedings before the trial Court is hereby exempted, however,
on condition that each of the petitioners/accused shall furnish undertaking by virtue of filing individual affidavits to the effect that their counsel shall remain present on each and every date of hearing before the trial Court, and shall not delay the proceedings by seeking adjournments.

The affidavit shall further clearly state that anything said by their lawyer(s) shall not be disputed by the petitioners at any state of the proceedings; and that in case their physical presence is required during the course of the proceedings before the trial Court, they shall Page No.# 5/5 appear as and when asked to do so.

I hereby make it clear that in case any of the conditions narrated above is violated by the petitioners,
the exemption from appearance before the trial Court shall be withdrawn without reference to this Court.
Let the affidavits be filed before the trial Court within 21 days from today.

13. The petition is disposed of with the above observations/provisions.
14. Let a copy of the order be provided under the signature of the Court Master.
